description:
Does AI change when companies should build their own software instead of buying it?

Kai Hendry and Vincent discuss Anthropic's Scion source-control system and what it suggests about enterprise SaaS, coding agents and the changing role of engineers. We look at infrastructure testing, saying no to over-engineered code, pair programming with agents, release approvals, and the fast-moving Bun, TypeScript and edge-runtime ecosystem.

AI Infrastructure — Episode 46
Recorded 14 October 2026.

CHAPTERS
00:00 AI, jobs and keeping up
03:04 Anthropic's Scion: rethinking source control
07:29 Agent Client Protocol and Kiro
10:29 Claude, Codex and agent harnesses
14:06 Engineers saying no to agents
17:58 Auditing tests that only test themselves
19:06 Infrastructure testing with Terraform and Terratest
27:46 Side agents, Claude Code mods and cmux
31:19 Rethinking merge queues and smoke tests
32:28 Build versus buy: is enterprise SaaS in trouble?
40:02 Pair programming when agents do the coding
46:49 Bun, Tov and the changing TypeScript toolchain
50:21 Security checks and enterprise release workflows
54:49 Separation of duties and agent approvals
1:03:40 Deno, Cloudflare and edge runtimes
1:09:17 Agent sandboxes and short-lived execution
1:14:00 Recap, model costs and closing tangents
